question: Does unreallabsai/unreal-agent carry machinery worth adopting into tezgah, and what would each piece cost to adopt?

evaluation.metric: candidates carried, not counted: every candidate that survives into findings.md names a file:line citation in the surveyed repository, the invariant it observes, the tezgah surface it would land on, and a verdict of adopt / adapt / reject with its cost; zero refusals from `bin/tezgah-research check --strict repo-adoption-unreal-agent`
evaluation.baseline: no run: the repository is cloned and read but never built, imported or executed; no binary is produced, no model call is made against it, nothing is installed; the line records no results row and therefore declares no scope - it holds twenty claims, none of them an evidence claim. No number in this line is a measurement of unreallabsai/unreal-agent or of tezgah; the deliverable is a reading pass over 169 Go files, not a behavioural metric
evaluation.locked_at: 2026-09-22, committed at c9a7243 with experiments/E1-repo-survey/protocol.md before any survey returned, so the prediction in that protocol is provably older than the candidates it is scored against; the criterion is a count over artifacts already agreed to be produced, not a pre-registered behavioural metric. No claim in this line reports a number this session measured.

environment.model: none (no model call was made against the repository; seven read-only surveys read files, and six arXiv records were confirmed through the arXiv API)

hypotheses: H1 (CONFIRMED as to direction, PARTIAL as to specifics): the adoptable material is the repository's decomposition discipline rather than its code. Confirmed by C02, C03, C05, C06, C07, C15 and C16 - every surviving candidate is a rule, a field or a paragraph, and no slice recommended porting the runtime. The specific mechanism named in the protocol, the tool-translator/operation split, is what carries the discipline, but the engine it feeds is rejected on the process-boundary axis by C01 and by 2608.28553.

H2 (PARTIALLY REFUTED): the prediction that the versioned forkable session store and the stable-id input dedup are the two subsystems tezgah most lacks and would most likely have to build rather than borrow. Refuted in one direction by C03 and C04 - the version gate is a key plus a branch and the identity rule is two to three files, so both are cheap adaptations rather than subsystems to build; and refuted outright on the fork half by C10, because the repository declares its own fork path unsound at harness/coordinator/loop.go:552, so it was never a borrowable source.

The prediction in experiments/E1-repo-survey/protocol.md scores PARTIAL: its falsifier - every surveyed subsystem reducing to 'requires a host tezgah does not have' - did not fire, since 28 of 36 candidates landed on a live tezgah surface (C19).

sessions.what: asked for a comprehensive survey of unreallabsai/unreal-agent as an adoption candidate for tezgah, with any method tezgah could implement, run through subagents and the research layer; no implementation, no commit to tezgah's own code

cloned the repository at commit b7c9bf1 (MIT, Go 1.27, 169 Go files, 61,771 lines under harness/ internal/ cmd/ benchmarks/) into .tezgah/scratch/unreal-agent, mapped its subsystems, and opened this line with the evaluation locked and experiments/E1-repo-survey/protocol.md committed at c9a7243 before any survey ran

fanned out seven read-only slices in one batch - coordinator+inbox, operations+primitives, context builder+tools, session store, llm+runner+benchmark+CI, the tezgah extension-surface map, and a shell-capable literature step - each required to cite file:line and to return candidates with a verdict and a cost; read the highest-signal files first-hand in parallel so the load-bearing claims could be re-checked

re-verified every tezgah-side claim before it entered a claim row (the absent format version, the validate-outside-the-lock order, the two readers' opposite postures on identical damage, the two timeout sites, the nine unpinned CI actions, the ledger's boolean failed) and confirmed all six arXiv records through the arXiv API independently of the notes that quote them, which corrected one category (2608.03836 is cs.LG, not cs.ML)

closed the line: seven literature notes with their INDEX.jsonl rows, twenty claims recorded through `tezgah-research claim` (never by editing claims.jsonl), findings.md with six sourced Patterns bullets, experiments/E1-repo-survey/analysis.md scoring the prediction PARTIAL, to_human/report.md with the nine ranked methods and what the survey does not establish, and to_human/review.json whose six findings each quote the file they target verbatim. Nothing was installed, run, benchmarked or measured, and no file in the clone was modified.

measured the report's five cost estimates against the running system's own stores rather than leaving them as guesses: 2592 evidence ledgers holding 57469 rows under ~/.cache/tezgah, this repository's 15 research lines and 268 claims, 2607 JSONL files, and the 91 commits touching plans/open. Recorded as C21-C24 and written into the report's Measured section. The measurement corrected three of the five estimates and weakened a fourth, because the outcome-less run rows are host-local (203 of 1276 sessions all-or-nothing, 5 mixed) rather than systematic. Implementing the surviving item then forced a full read of its cut site and withdrew the line's own top finding: open_plans already appends a marker, recorded as the refuted C23c. One item of the five was actionable, not two. This is the line's only measured work, and its scope is real recorded data, not a fixture.

implemented the one surviving item: .github/workflows/ci.yml now pins all nine uses lines to commit SHAs with their tags in trailing comments, declares permissions: {} at the top and contents: read per job, and sets persist-credentials: false on all four checkouts. Verified by parsing the committed file (9 uses lines, 0 unpinned, 0 mutable tags, 4 persist-credentials, four jobs each scoped) and by running the repository's own suite. Nothing else from the survey was implemented; the remaining candidates stay estimates in the report.
